extracted.intended_audience: comedians, sketch writers, TV creators, and critics studying/replicating Nathan Fielder's awkward-silence comedic style
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for creating comedy in the vein of Nathan Fielder: a committed awkward persona interacting with real people, using prolonged silence, deadpan sincerity, and destabilizing remarks to elicit authentic reactions. Emphasizes format, tactics, ethical considerations, and why the approach works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core Persona — committed awkward loner
rubrics_metrics.description: Awkward loner. Blank stare. Seeming inability to respond to social cues. Generates one deeply uncomfortable moment after another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Play a slightly off, socially inept version of yourself (or a constructed persona) and commit fully. The persona should consistently behave as if earnest rather than knowingly comedic; do not wink or break character. The persona itself is the joke — maintain consistency across situations to escalate discomfort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format — real people + outlandish proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Plays a slightly more awkward fictional version of himself; offers absurd/expensive business advice to real businesses; real subjects, real reactions; Fielder maintains the persona without breaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use authentic settings and non-actor subjects whenever possible to preserve genuine reaction. Structure bits around delivering an outlandish, seemingly sincere proposal to a real business or person (e.g., elaborate publicity stunts). Maintain production realism so subjects treat the situation as legitimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Excruciating Silence — use of prolonged silence
rubrics_metrics.description: Willing to let things get more excruciatingly awkward than most people have a tolerance for; willing to sit silently for long periods to the point that the people he's interacting with are forced to reveal themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intentionally hold silence after a prompt/question to pressure the other person into filling the gap; tolerate audience and subject discomfort. Anti-pattern: cutting the silence too quickly or using silence without a clear purpose, which can deflate the bit instead of revealing character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disrupting Small Talk — destabilizing via bizarre but nonrude comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Makes bizarre comments without rudeness; destabilizes interviewees; gets authentic reactions in an age of careful 'reality' TV.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce odd, unexpected observations or questions that are not plainly hostile — the goal is to unsettle and reveal, not to insult. Keep tone neutral/earnest so the comment reads as sincere rather than confrontational.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sincerity Mode — never break character or wink
rubrics_metrics.description: Never winks at the camera. Always 'earnest.' The persona is the joke, but persona never breaks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain deadpan, unwavering earnestness even as suggestions escalate in absurdity. Avoid meta-comments, knowing looks, or signaling to the audience that the persona is performative; maintain straighfaced commitment to the premise throughout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real reactions as the comedic engine
rubrics_metrics.description: The audience watches Fielder break others. Or, more often, watches the others reveal genuine warmth/weirdness. The comedy comes from authentic reaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design situations that put real people in states where their unrehearsed responses are likely to surface. Avoid over-staging or coaching reactions; prioritize setups that create psychological pressure (silence, odd proposals) to generate truthfully messy human behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gap-driven humor — contrast between stilted persona and outlandish suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: Comedy comes from the gap between Fielder's stilted demeanor and his outlandish suggestions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amplify contrast: keep delivery flat and earnest while the content of proposals becomes increasingly absurd. The cognitive dissonance between delivery and content is the source of humor—escalate content while keeping tone constant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject ethics and editing choices
rubrics_metrics.description: Real people involved. Some debate over consent / manipulation. Fielder generally edits to make subjects sympathetic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful of consent and the moral implications of manufacturing awkwardness with non-actors. If using real people, consider pre- or post-consent practices, and use editing choices responsibly (e.g., shaping narrative to avoid exploitative portrayals). Anticipate critique about manipulation and plan safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature tactical checklist (Fielder-style rubric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit five-question rubric: 1) Is there a committed awkward persona? 2) Are real people / situations involved? 3) Is silence used as a tool? 4) Is the sincerity uncracked? 5) Does the comedy come from authentic reaction?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this checklist as a quick pre-release audit for a bit. If any item is missing, reconsider the setup: e.g., if reactions are staged, you lose the core engine; if sincerity is cracked, the contrast disappears. The checklist condenses the essay's principles into actionable yes/no criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tactical example bank (notable bits as models)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notable bits cited as exemplars: 'Dumb Starbucks' (replicating Starbucks with 'Dumb' prefix), the Holocaust survivor / petting zoo bit, the pig saving a goat in the lake (manufactured).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study these concrete examples to see how format, persona, silence, and editing combine. Use similar high-concept premises anchored in low-key delivery. Extract practical lessons (e.g., how an elaborate stunt can be framed as earnest advice) rather than copying specifics.
